purpose: Small, diverse, provenance-bearing external knowledge foundation for shadow review; never a production rule set.

records.normalized_claim: Light can be composed through controllable properties rather than intensity alone, so hierarchy is a contextual design choice.
exclusions: Does not identify the visual priority of an unobserved rig.
Does not prescribe a fixture family or color.
conflicts: Hierarchy may be organized through contrast, direction, focus, density, or stillness.
records.source_provenance: ETC_EDUCATIONAL_RESOURCES: derived from educational coverage of controllable properties of light.
records.summary: Use as a review lens for an intentional main visual relationship, not as an action recipe.

records.normalized_claim: Color is one controllable property among several and should serve the performance context rather than carry a fixed emotional meaning by itself.
exclusions: Does not require a dominant color.
Does not treat multicolor as inherently wrong.
conflicts: Camera, scenic material, performer visibility, and fixture gamut can constrain color decisions.
records.summary: Supports palette-coherence review without a palette recipe.

records.normalized_claim: Movement in space is a compositional property that can be selected for a performance purpose, not an automatic consequence of mover availability.
exclusions: Does not require movement in every high-energy section.
Requires verified movement capability and safe spatial context.
conflicts: A static composition can be the stronger contextual choice.
records.summary: A reason is required before movement becomes a strategy.

records.normalized_claim: Lighting design can serve both functional readability and artistic storytelling, so visual attention should be evaluated against the performance need.
exclusions: Does not prove performer position or acting area.
Does not authorize focus actions without targets.
conflicts: Environmental or silhouette emphasis can be intentional alternatives to subject focus.
records.summary: Focus remains a visual intention until target semantics are verified.

records.normalized_claim: Multiple controllable properties can change a visual state, so density should be reviewed as composition rather than equated with fixture count or dimmer level.
exclusions: Does not require more layers at higher energy.
Does not establish coverage or visual weight of current Groups.
conflicts: A sparse state can be a complete designed look.
records.summary: Use to inspect all-equal density cohorts without assuming a replacement.

records.normalized_claim: Tracking and stored cue values must remain inspectable so a programmer can distinguish a local cue change from a tracked consequence.
exclusions: Does not prescribe a lighting look.
Does not authorize direct console edits in this knowledge pack.
conflicts: Cue-only versus tracking is an implementation decision governed by the workflow contract.
records.summary: Supports Focus Execute and operator handover review.

records.normalized_claim: Content and tracking views support operator inspection of stored values, effects, and cue flow; native editability is distinct from merely achieving visible output.
exclusions: Does not establish an optimal sequence architecture.
Does not make agent internals acceptable inside the Show.
conflicts: The stable operator contract governs user-facing structure.
records.summary: Provides a technical review lens for maintainable implementation.

records.normalized_claim: A fixture definition can contain multiple DMX modes tied to software versions, so capability claims require an exact mode/version binding.
exclusions: A library filename similarity is not a loaded-Show binding.
Technical capability is not artistic role eligibility.
conflicts: A Show-bound exported profile can outrank an unbound external candidate.
records.summary: Reinforces the existing Show-bound FixtureType binding boundary.

records.normalized_claim: Channel attributes and mode-specific channel functions describe technical control possibilities, but they do not determine whether a visual function is appropriate for a song or section.
exclusions: Does not infer geometry, coverage, or audience viewpoint.
Does not turn a Group label into a permanent role.
conflicts: Action grammar and spatial semantics can still block a technically available attribute.
records.summary: Technical inventory must remain separate from case selection.

records.normalized_claim: Fixture-definition revisions and real-fixture test tags have distinct provenance, so profile evidence should retain revision and verification status.
exclusions: A community revision is not equivalent to real-console verification.
Does not establish Show identity.
conflicts: Manufacturer, real-fixture-tested, and work-in-progress status have different evidentiary weight.
records.summary: Supports provenance preservation for future external fixture knowledge.

records.normalized_claim: One immersive-production designer describes balancing energy and emotion through contrast between quiet scenes and high-octane musical numbers.
exclusions: Not a rule that every song must drop energy between peaks.
Not transferable without song and production context.
conflicts: Sustained energy or gradual transitions can be equally valid.
records.source_provenance: PLASA_PARADISE_UNDER_THE_STARS: designer statement reported in trade press.
records.summary: Case evidence for contrast as an available strategy, not a mandatory curve.

records.normalized_claim: Quiet scenes can be intentionally contrasted with high-energy material when the production's emotional arc benefits from that relationship.
exclusions: Does not define low energy as incomplete.
Does not prescribe a fixed verse/refrain pattern.
conflicts: A quiet scene can also use dense or active visual detail.
records.summary: Supports contextual review of intentional visual rest.

records.normalized_claim: A production's lighting can participate in an emotional arc through designed relationships between scenes rather than isolated cue decisions.
exclusions: Does not impose a monotonic A-to-B-to-C progression.
Does not replace real song analysis.
conflicts: Non-linear arcs, plateaus, resets, and repeated identities remain valid.
records.summary: A contextual support for whole-show relationships.

records.normalized_claim: A touring case describes color, movement, and shape changing continuously to follow nuanced musical change; the relationship is case-specific rather than a universal palette recipe.
exclusions: Does not require continuous change.
Does not prescribe any specific color or genre language.
conflicts: Intentional palette continuity can be stronger than constant variation.
records.summary: An industry reference for relating visual change to musical nuance.

records.normalized_claim: A documented touring design used a continuous spectrum of movement, shape, and color change to maintain variety while tracking musical nuance.
exclusions: Does not make motion mandatory.
Does not apply where position/movement action grammar is unavailable.
conflicts: Stillness can intentionally create emphasis or contrast.
records.summary: A case-specific example of movement as relationship, not automatic texture.

records.normalized_claim: Variety can be maintained through contextually related visual changes across a show, but a source case does not justify forcing every repeated section to differ.
exclusions: Does not require repeat escalation.
Does not prefer novelty over intentional similarity.
conflicts: Repeated identity can be the purposeful design decision.
records.summary: Supports review of meaningful rather than automatic repeated-section variation.

records.normalized_claim: A camera-oriented music-video case used a limited palette as one strategy for its song and branding context, not as evidence that multicolor is bad.
exclusions: Does not require minimal color.
Does not establish a personal preference or global color rule.
conflicts: Other designs may benefit from broad or changing palettes.
records.source_provenance: PLASA_CHAUVET_CHURCH_VIDEO: designer statement in a single documented case.
records.summary: Explicitly guards against MULTICOLOR_EQUALS_BAD.

records.normalized_claim: A documented music-video case used intense brightness and sudden darkness as a context-specific contrast mechanism for instrumental material.
exclusions: Does not make blackout a default drop behavior.
Does not make high impact continuously desirable.
conflicts: Transitions may instead be gradual, color-led, or static.
records.source_provenance: PLASA_CHAUVET_CHURCH_VIDEO: designer statement in a single documented case.
records.summary: Alternative mechanism for punctuation, pending song/camera context.

records.normalized_claim: Strobing and intensity variation were used in one documented production for selected instrumental context; timing remains an available mechanism rather than an energy-level requirement.
exclusions: Does not infer safe strobe behavior from a Group label.
Does not require timing on a drop or high-energy section.
conflicts: High-energy sustained sections may intentionally omit punctuation.
records.summary: Reinforces existing B3 separation of energy and timing.

records.normalized_claim: A high-energy visual case used darkness and silhouette as part of its contrast language, illustrating that an intentional omission can be a positive compositional decision.
exclusions: Does not make darkness or silhouette appropriate without context.
Requires visual/camera evidence before application.
conflicts: Readability needs can outweigh silhouette intent.
records.summary: Supports omission as a candidate strategy, never a preset look.

records.normalized_claim: Color, direction, shape, edge, and movement are separable design dimensions that may be combined or withheld to build visual depth.
exclusions: Does not require all dimensions in one look.
Does not establish physical depth without Show geometry.
conflicts: A deliberately flat or singular image can be contextually appropriate.
records.summary: Layering is a vocabulary for comparison, not a layer-count ladder.

records.normalized_claim: Because visual state can change through multiple dimensions, a design may reserve some available dimensions for later contrast instead of activating every resource immediately.
exclusions: Does not require saving resources for a final chorus.
Does not define a universal hierarchy among fixtures.
conflicts: A sustained fully developed state can be appropriate when context supports it.
records.source_provenance: ETC_EDUCATIONAL_RESOURCES: bounded inference from multiple controllable properties.
records.summary: A shadow review hypothesis, not a source-mandated rule.

records.normalized_claim: A restrained visual state can still be intentionally composed through focus, color, direction, shape, edge, or stillness rather than being only a reduced-intensity version of another look.
exclusions: Does not require every dimension to be available.
Does not prescribe minimalism as a preference.
conflicts: A low-energy state can also be visually active when song context supports it.
records.summary: Aligns with existing human-confirmed complete-look evidence without replacing it.

records.normalized_claim: Fixture technical data may describe channels and geometries, but audience-facing composition still depends on an actual rig's verified placement and relationships.
exclusions: Does not infer left/right, stage axes, coverage, or dominance from fixture identity.
Does not replace a venue or visual survey.
conflicts: Synthetic semantic rig data may be used only when explicitly supplied.

records.normalized_claim: A touring case used changing visual dimensions to keep pace with musical nuance; resource use should therefore be assessed for contextual function, not simply availability.
exclusions: Does not make every available role active.
Does not establish a fixture priority order.
conflicts: Limited rigs may combine functions or deliberately omit dimensions.

records.normalized_claim: Lighting can guide attention by controlling where visual information is concentrated within a larger stage image.

Does not require one dominant fixture.
conflicts: A deliberately distributed image may be appropriate.

records.normalized_claim: Changes in direction, intensity, color, or shape can redirect audience attention without requiring every other area to change.

Requires actual visual context.
conflicts: Continuity may be preferable to redirection.

records.normalized_claim: A lighting composition can frame an area of action so the audience understands its relative importance.

Does not require a followspot.
conflicts: The whole stage may intentionally share attention.

records.normalized_claim: Attention can be shaped by contrast between a selected area and its surroundings rather than by making the selected area universally bright.

records.normalized_claim: Color can separate visual areas or connect them, depending on the relationship between palette, direction, and composition.

records.normalized_claim: Separating front, middle, and back visual information can create depth when the physical relationships support it.

records.normalized_claim: Movement can establish direction and spatial relationship, but a still image can be the more meaningful contrast.

records.normalized_claim: A whole-show energy arc can be shaped through relationships between states rather than by assigning every section an absolute intensity rank.

records.normalized_claim: A lower-intensity state can still be complete when its focus, palette, texture, and negative space form an intentional composition.

records.normalized_claim: A repeated section can retain identity while changing one relationship that reflects a changed transition, emphasis, or surrounding context.
